findings.F1: The book fails on its falls, not its gain: its Calmar is 0.71 against the rule's 0.75, from a +8.0 % yearly return and a deepest fall of −8.5 % in w17; 372 of the 474 days spent more than 3 % under the peak fall in w15 to w18 (90, 101, 103 and 78 days).
findings.F2: All of the book's gain comes from positions held while the coin's 60-day return was above +10 %. In that rising trend, 815 held bars earned +0.29 % each, +2.38 summed. Held bars in the other trends earned nothing: falling 716 bars at −0.006 % each (−0.05 summed), choppy 199 bars at −0.06 % each (−0.12 summed). So 915 of the 1,730 held bars added risk without gain.
findings.F3: Fresh 20-day-high breaks are followed by a much larger 5-day unusual move in a rising 60-day trend than in the others. Rising: +5.3 %, t 3.49, 109 cases. Choppy: +2.9 %, t 1.34, 32 cases. Falling: +0.5 %, t 0.27, 30 cases. A rising trend alone does not carry this move: grid bars without a break in a rising trend give +0.6 % (t 0.82, 288 cases), so the trend limits where the breakout effect holds and is not an effect of its own. This fits the brief's theory that breakout and trend-following flows add to a coin already being read as trending.
findings.F4: During the book's deep falls (more than 3 % under the peak), only 18 % of the held bars were in a rising 60-day trend, against 27 % of all held bars. The falls are made disproportionately by positions taken outside the rising trend.
findings.F5: The size of the move is not the problem: the total move per case is +2.34 %, 12.1 times the 0.19 % cost of a trade. Held bars 0 to 5 days after the fresh break earn +0.39 %, −0.13 %, +0.39 %, +0.25 %, +0.38 % and +0.23 % a bar. Bars 6 or more days after the break (1,093 held bars) earn about 0 (−0.04 % and −0.008 % a bar), so the aged positions only add swings.
findings.F6: Breaks out of a narrow range carry the effect and breaks out of a wide one do not. By the prior 20-day range width (high minus low, over price), the 5-day unusual move after a fresh break is +3.3 % (t 2.92) in the narrowest third, +4.1 % (t 2.56) in the middle third and +1.1 % (t 0.76) in the widest third, with 92 to 93 cases each. Without a break, the same thirds give +0.5 % (t 1.31), −0.6 % and −0.5 %, so a narrow range alone is not the effect.
findings.F7: Breaks made while the coin's recent swing is high against its longer swing (30-day over 60-day daily standard deviation) carry more. By thirds of that ratio, the unusual move is +2.3 % (t 1.50), +4.7 % (t 2.90) and +5.1 % (t 2.04), with 57 cases each. Held bars by the same thirds earn −0.01 %, +0.10 % and +0.30 % a bar. Without a break the ratio shows no pattern (−0.8 %, +1.1 %, −1.4 %), so the swing alone is not the effect.

ideas.idea: In a rising market, when a coin closes above its 20-day high, it rises over the next 5 days, and it rises more the further the close sits above that high, with the rise completed within those 5 days of the break rather than continuing while the close stays above the range.
ideas.consequence: A trader buys 20-day-high breaks only in coins whose 60-day trend is rising, sized by the break's distance and given back after 5 days, and refuses the same breaks in choppy or falling coins where they made the falls without the gain.
ideas.name: rising-market upside break hold

ideas.idea: When a coin closes above its 20-day high, it rises over the next 5 days, and it rises more the narrower its 20-day high-to-low range was against its price before the break, with the rise completed within those 5 days.
ideas.consequence: A trader weights a 20-day-high break by how tight the range it escapes was, taking breaks of narrow ranges with size and breaks of already wide ranges with little or none.
ideas.name: narrow-range upside break hold

ideas.idea: When a coin closes above its 20-day high, it rises over the next 5 days, and it rises more the larger its last 30 days' swing is against its swing over the 60 days before the break, with the rise completed within those 5 days.
ideas.consequence: A trader sizes a 20-day-high break up when the coin has lately been swinging more than over its past two months and down when it has been quieter, cutting the breaks that carried little gain into the book's falls.
ideas.name: agitated upside break hold
